title: Electricity sources in Calderon
prompt: The line graph shows the share of electricity that Calderon generated from three sources between 1995 and 2020. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

chart.title: Share of electricity generated by source, Calderon, 1995 to 2020

sentences.text: The line graph illustrates changes in the share of electricity that Calderon generated from coal, gas and renewable sources between 1995 and 2020.
sentences.why: Paraphrases the prompt with illustrates, changes in the share and generated from, so it avoids copying the question and earns Lexical Resource. It contains no figures, as an introduction should.

sentences.text: Overall, the contribution of coal fell steadily throughout the period, whereas renewable energy grew at an increasingly rapid rate.
sentences.why: Names the two main trends with no numbers. Whereas contrasts opposite directions, and increasingly rapid rate describes the shape of the growth, which is what Task Achievement rewards in an overview.

sentences.text: Furthermore, renewables, which began as the smallest source, had become the largest by 2020.
sentences.why: Adds the extreme at the end of the period and the change in rank. A non-defining relative clause shows grammatical range, and no data appears, so the overview stays general.

sentences.text: Renewable sources supplied only 5 per cent of electricity in 1995, far less than coal at 55 per cent and gas at 30 per cent.
sentences.why: Opens with the starting point of the rising trend and places it against the other two sources. Far less than gives a precise comparison, and the three figures match the graph.

sentences.text: This share rose slowly to 12 per cent in 2005 before accelerating sharply, reaching 40 per cent in 2015 and 58 per cent in 2020.
sentences.why: Tracks the whole rise in one sentence and changes the verb to show speed: slowly, then accelerating sharply. The key years and values are accurate, which supports Task Achievement and range.

sentences.text: By 2015, renewables had therefore overtaken both coal and gas, which stood at 15 and 38 per cent respectively.
sentences.why: Reports the cross-over with the past perfect, had overtaken, and uses respectively to give two figures accurately. Therefore links the sentence to the growth just described for Coherence.

sentences.text: Gas also expanded at first, peaking at 42 per cent in 2010.
sentences.why: A short sentence that places the gas trend with the rising group and names its peak. Peaking at is a natural trend phrase, and the year and figure are correct.

sentences.text: In contrast, coal was the source in steady decline.
sentences.why: A short contrast topic sentence that signals the shift to falling trends. In contrast is an accurate linker, and the paragraph now has one clear theme for Coherence and Cohesion.

sentences.text: Its share fell from 55 per cent in 1995 to 40 per cent in 2005, level with gas at that point, and then to just 7 per cent in 2020.
sentences.why: Gives the start, the middle point and the end of the coal line. Level with gas notes the intersection, and just before the final figure shows how small the share became.

sentences.text: Gas, meanwhile, dropped back from its 2010 peak to 31 per cent in 2020, leaving it 27 percentage points behind renewables.
sentences.why: Completes the gas trend and makes a final comparison with the leader. The gap of 27 is correct, and percentage points is the exact term for a difference between two percentages.

sentences.text: Coal, therefore, ended the period with the smallest contribution of the three.
sentences.why: A closing fact that is true from the graph and uses a superlative. It adds no opinion or explanation, which Task 1 does not allow, and it rounds off the second body paragraph.

analysis: The instruction is to select and report the main features and make comparisons. Three lines and six years mean you must group trends, not narrate every point.
Group by direction: renewables rose throughout, coal fell throughout, and gas rose and then fell. Gas is the line that changes direction, so mention its peak at 42 per cent in 2010.
Look for intersections. Coal and gas are level at 40 per cent in 2005, and renewables overtake gas between 2010 and 2015, so a cross-over belongs in the overview or in the body.
Paraphrase: "shows" becomes illustrates; "share of electricity" becomes proportion of electricity; "generated from" can stay; "between 1995 and 2020" becomes over the 25-year period.
Use past tenses throughout, because every date is past. Past perfect (had overtaken) is correct for an event completed before a later date.

Turkish L1 watch: students often write "58 percent" or "the 58 per cent" and drop articles before superlatives ("became largest source" instead of "became the largest source"). Check every superlative has the.
Do not explain why coal fell, and do not predict the future. The graph gives no reasons, and Task 1 asks for an objective report only.

plan.idea: Paraphrase only: the graph illustrates changes in the share of electricity from coal, gas and renewables between 1995 and 2020.
Coal fell steadily and renewables grew faster and faster; renewables began smallest and ended largest. No figures.
Renewables 5, 12, 40, 58 per cent; overtook coal and gas by 2015. Gas rose to a peak of 42 per cent in 2010.
Coal 55, 40, 7 per cent, level with gas in 2005. Gas fell to 31 per cent, 27 points behind renewables.
